- Large V-shaped/wedge yellowing (chlorosis) from the leaf margin inward
- Brown necrotic tip/margin
- A few small dark lesions within the chlorotic zone
- No concentric rings, no fuzzy growth, no small distinct spots

This strongly suggests **Verticillium_Wilt** (V-shaped lesion widest at margin with brown necrosis). Let me check reference images for my top candidates.

This Verticillium reference shows wilting but not the sharp V-shaped margin chlorosis. Let me check another Verticillium reference and also examine Early_Blight and Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus to compare.
This second Verticillium reference shows yellow-green with brown necrosis - very similar to the test image pattern. Now let me check Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus for comparison.
TSWV shows bronzing with small spots - clearly different from the test image. For my last view, I'll check Early_Blight to rule it out.

The Early_Blight reference shows discrete dark lesions with concentric rings scattered across the leaf - clearly different from the test image's pattern.

**Summary of evidence:**

| Feature | Test Image | Best Match |
|---|---|---|
| Pattern | Large V-shaped yellowing from leaf margin | Verticillium_Wilt |
| Necrosis | Brown tip/margin | Verticillium_Wilt |
| Lesion type | Diffuse chlorosis, no concentric rings | Rules out Early_Blight |
| No bronzing/spots | Diffuse marginal pattern | Rules out TSWV |

The test image shows the classic **Verticillium_Wilt** V-shaped leaf lesion: yellowing widest at the leaf margin tapering inward, with brown necrotic tissue at the tip, exactly matching the KB description: "V-shaped leaf lesions widest at the leaf margin, brown necrotic tissue surrounded by irregular yellowing."
